name: DOOM Music Extension
author: Thomas Reetz

provenance.from: kyzer.me.uk/amos/amosfactory/dme.lha, retrieved 2026-08-12 and held in the corpus at sources/kyzer-dme/. 692,668 bytes, sha256 e9f0baa035f6c38606bb6d6ccad4924d1e33b03e206a6c6ca31dc949c3312338 -- the "676Kb - LhA" the AMOS extension list promised. That list's own download link was lha/dme.lha on amigau.com and the Wayback Machine never captured it; kyzer's AMOS Factory mirror had it.
provenance.note: SLOT 15, AND THE BINARY SAYS SO: routine 0 stores its AllocMem'd block with `move.l d0,$1d8(a5)` and returns `moveq #$e,d0`, and ($1d8-$f8)/16+1 is 15 on the ExtAdr layout (+Equ.s:1185) with $e the slot zero-based. Jens Vang Petersen's AMOS extension pages, 1997-1998, said 15 too, and also record "PRO Version: 2.00", no TC version, and Public Domain. IT REFUSES TO LOAD ANYWHERE ELSE: the first instruction after the register save is `cmp.l #$41506578,d1` --- the ASCII `APex` --- and a mismatch returns -1 without allocating anything.
provenance.redistribution: Public Domain per the extension list. Not redistributed by amos-ts; fixtures/ is gitignored.

findings: REPLACES AN AMOSTOOLS STUB. Until 2026-08-12 this row held only the token table with the library stripped out from under it -- both length fields zero, no code, every routine word overwritten with `====` -- so the tier could not rise above `manual`. The real library's table is IDENTICAL to the stub's, entry for entry, id for id and spec for spec, which is a check on the AMOSTools reader as much as on this registration. What changes is that the code is now here to read. 233 entries, 184 distinct names, and 36 rows literally called `nop` -- padding between the blocks, one per replayer, so a later version can add a keyword without moving anybody's ids. THIRTEEN REPLAYERS IN ONE LIBRARY, each with the same shape of load/play/stop/cont/volume/song pos/patt pos/vu: `dmed` (MED), `omed` (OctaMED), `omix` (OctaMIX, with a 14-bit mode), `sid`, `ptm` (ProTracker, and the only one with a CIA speed), `thx`, `p61`, `fc13`, `fc14`, `smon` (SoundMon), `sfx13`, `db` (DigiBooster, with a mixer and a boost rate), `tfmx`, `s3m` and `xm`, plus a `dme sam *` sampler. It shares four `p61 *` names with the registered P61 extension and all six `thx *` names with THX 0.6, and shares NOT ONE ID with either -- which is what made the cataloguer score on ids rather than names. THE ARCHIVE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE EXTENSION: libs/ holds ELEVEN FORMAT REPLAYERS as separate Amiga libraries, all dated 3 Nov 1997 -- DME_FastTracker (XM, 26,324 bytes), DME_OctaMix (24,140), DME_Med (15,448), DME_ScreamTracker (S3M, 13,844), DME_OctaMed (13,244), DME_DigiBooster (13,080), DME_TFMX (9,544), DME_FC1.3 (6,460), DME_FC1.4 (6,212), DME_SoundMon2.0 (4,520) and DME_SoundFX1.3 (3,476). This port has protracker.ts and p61.ts and nothing else, so that is the reading material for every other tracker format in the corpus whether or not this row is ever ported. Note which formats have EXAMPLES but no library: Protracker, P61, PlaySid and THX are either built in or expected from LIBS: -- settle it from this library's own OpenLibrary calls, not from the file list. Its error strings ("Can't load DME_OctaMix.library V2.0 or higher") show the loading is per-format and versioned. WHICH FORMATS ARE INTERNAL IS NOW SETTLED FROM THE BINARY rather than from the file list, which is what the row asked for. Twelve library names appear in the hunk, each with its own versioned error string: DME_OctaMix, DME_OctaMed, DME_Med, DME_TFMX, DME_ScreamTracker, DME_FC1.3, DME_FC1.4, DME_SoundMon2.0, DME_SoundFX1.3, DME_FastTracker, DME_DigiBooster and playsid. The blocks with NO library name and no load error are exactly four --- `ptm`, `thx`, `p61` and `dme sam` --- which is the guide's own Internal-Player column to the entry. So Protracker, THX, Player 6.1A and sample replay are in these 46,208 bytes and everything else is a separate binary in `libs/`. THAT IS ALSO THE PART THIS PORT CAN ALREADY PLAY, because protracker.ts, thxplay.ts, p61.ts and the sample path are all here: 14 + 13 + 10 + 6 keywords, plus the 37 `nop` rows, is 80 of the 220 named entries. `nop` IS AN `rts` --- routine 38 is one instruction and all 37 rows point at it --- so the padding costs nothing to be faithful about. THE FOUR BLOCKS SHARE ONE SHAPE: `X Load file$,bank` (spec `I2,0`, and the bank number pops FIRST), `X Play bank`, `X Stop`, `X Cont`, `X Volume n`, `=X Song Pos`, `=X Patt Pos`, `=X Vu(n)`, `=X Song Length`, with `X Next Patt`/`X Prev Patt` where the format has patterns. `Ptm Load` checks the module's magic at $438 for `M.K.`, `M!K!` or `FLT4` and nothing else, so a 15-instrument or 31-instrument tag it does not know is refused. `Ptm Cia Speed` is the only CIA-tempo keyword in the extension. PLAYSID IS A WALL and the guide says why in its own words: "To keep the full copyright of this format we didn't enclose the playsid.library". It is the one external format with no binary anywhere in the archive.
notes: Plays OctaMED, ProTracker and several other module formats, one set of keywords per format.
